provenance.derivation: Composed in the manner of kasane no irome, for summer: 3 of our own published entries read as layers from the outermost inward — 錆銅 sabi-do, then 岩清水 iwa-shimizu, then 夜紙 yoru-gami. NOT a historical combination: no layer is asserted to reproduce a documented Heian kasane, and no value was read from any kasane table. Chosen by hand, not generated. Every adjacent pair of layers is more than ΔE00 5 apart — the distance below which the product calls two items the same (FR-44) — because a layering whose edges cannot be told apart is not one; gate 11 recomputes that under the current engine on every run, so no figure is typed here. Weights fall inward (1, 0.8, 0.6) because each inner layer shows less than the one over it.
provenance.editorialNotes: High summer answered with cool: a weathered-copper green (錆銅) outermost, a pale spring-water layer (岩清水) that lifts it at the edge, and a near-black lining (夜紙) that gives both something to sit on. The lightness swings hard between layers, which is what makes a summer layering read in strong light. The name is ours (涼影, "Cool Shade"), coined as a seasonal image the way the historical names are; it is not presented as a traditional kasane name.
